headline: Steady growth as pricing gains offset softer volumes
summary_short: SiteOne's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 4.7% y/y to $1,530.7 million as gross margin expanded 50bp to 36.9%, lifting net income 8.0% y/y to $139.3 million and diluted EPS to $3.14.
summary_long: Growth was mostly acquisition-driven (3 of the 5 points of net-sales growth); Organic Daily Sales rose just 1% as roughly 3% price inflation offset softer new-residential and repair/upgrade demand. Gross margin gained 50bp on price realization and commercial initiatives, partially offset by higher freight, the new fifth distribution center, and commodity deflation. SG&A rose 6% on acquisition integration and higher healthcare costs. The company repurchased $113.8M of stock through the first half (plus $10.0M in July) and spent $40.6M on capex. Management reiterated full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $425-455 million. Long-term debt rose $121.5M on seasonal working-capital needs, acquisitions, and buybacks.

The FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range ($425M-$455M, reaffirmed) comes from SiteOne's July 29, 2026 earnings press release, not the 10-Q itself; direct fetches of businesswire.com, a Morningstar mirror, and investors.siteone.com all failed (403/404/timeout after 3 attempts), so this figure was extracted from a WebSearch synthesis of the release rather than read verbatim — confidence on that specific figure is set lower (0.75) in the shard's guidance entry and it should be re-verified against the primary release when reachable.

drivers.explanation: Q2 growth in net sales and Adjusted EBITDA came despite softer end markets, per CEO Doug Black; acquisitions (led by Reinders) performed well and the deal pipeline remains active.
Increase driven primarily by acquisitions (3 points); Organic Daily Sales +1% on ~3% price inflation, partially offset by softer new-residential and repair/upgrade demand.
Margin gain from price realization and commercial initiatives, partially offset by higher freight/distribution costs from fuel inflation, the new fifth distribution center, and commodity deflation.
Increase primarily due to improved gross margin, partially offset by lower sales volume and higher SG&A.
